question.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}9{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,-2\le y\le -1\}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:        

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}9{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}[{\int }_{1}^{2}9{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}[{\int }_{1}^{2}9{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}9{y}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}9{y}^{2}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{1}^{2}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}9{y}^{2}(\frac{{2}^{3}}{3}-\frac{{1}^{3}}{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}9{y}^{2}\cdot \frac{7}{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}21{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}21{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y & =21{[\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{-2}^{-1} \\  & =21(\frac{(-1)^{3}}{3}-\frac{(-2)^{3}}{3}) \\  & =49\end{aligned}
$$
